Shrunken group effects from a multilevel model

Source: R/val.R
val_group_effects.Rd

Extracts each group's random intercept from a multilevel model fitted with lme4, with its conditional standard error, an interval, the number of observations in the group and a flag for intervals that exclude zero. Used to find the groups, such as counties, where an outcome is higher or lower than the model's fixed part predicts.

Usage

val_group_effects(model, group, level = 0.9)

Arguments

model

A model fitted with lme4::lmer() or lme4::glmer() (class merMod) that has a random intercept for group.

group

The name of a grouping factor in model, bare or quoted, as it appears in the random-effects term, for example county in (1 | county).

level

Coverage of the interval, between 0 and 1.

Value

A tibble with one row per group, sorted from the largest effect to the smallest: the group (in a column named after group), estimate, std_error, lower, upper, n (observations used in the fit) and excludes_zero.

Details

A multilevel model gives each group its own intercept, drawn from a common normal distribution whose spread the model estimates. The intercepts returned here are the conditional modes (lme4::ranef()): each group's raw deviation pulled toward zero, more strongly when the group has few observations or the groups differ little. This pull is called shrinkage.

std_error is the conditional standard deviation from lme4::ranef(condVar = TRUE). It treats the fixed effects and the variance of the intercepts as known, so the intervals are somewhat too narrow. For lme4::glmer() fits the effects are on the scale of the link function, such as log odds for a logistic model.

The flag excludes_zero is a screening device, not a test. With many groups, some intervals will exclude zero by chance, so raise level when screening many groups.

Examples

fit <- lme4::lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = lme4::sleepstudy)
val_group_effects(fit, Subject)
